answer: Sustaining that many identities means writing fresh texts against a target that moves every epoch, and therefore the work cannot be batched or cached in advance. The lantern receipt proves which words were live for that identity, and the audit replays it against the seed. A pre-written answer bank therefore goes stale within one epoch, and reusing one text across 72 aliases trips the duplicate check at the signal gate. That is 13 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
